In [[circuit complexity]], '''AC''' is a [[complexity class]] hierarchy.  Each class, '''AC<sup>i</sup>''', consists of the [[formal language|languages]] recognized by [[Boolean circuit]]s with depth <math>O(\log^i n)</math> and a [[polynomial|polynomial number]] of [[fanin|unlimited fan-in]] [[AND gate|AND]] and [[OR gate]]s.

The name "AC" was chosen by analogy to [[NC (complexity)|NC]], with the "A" in the name standing for "alternating" and referring both to the alternation between the AND and OR gates in the circuits and to [[alternating Turing machine]]s.{{sfnp|Regan|1999|p=27-18}}

The smallest AC class is [[AC0|AC<sup>0</sup>]], consisting of constant-depth unlimited fan-in circuits.

The total hierarchy of AC classes is defined as
<blockquote>
<math>\mbox{AC} = \bigcup_{i \geq 0} \mbox{AC}^i</math> 
</blockquote>

==Relation to NC==
The AC classes are related to [[NC (complexity)|NC]], [[ACC (complexity)|ACC]], and [[TC (complexity)|TC]] classes. For each ''i'', we have<ref>{{harvtxt|Clote|Kranakis|2002}}, p. 437; {{harvtxt|Arora|Barak|2009}}, p. 118.</ref>

:<math>\mathsf{NC}^i \subseteq \mathsf{AC}^i \subseteq \mathsf{ACC}^{i}  \subseteq \mathsf{TC}^{i} \subseteq \mathsf{NC}^{i+1}.</math>

As an immediate consequence of this, we have that NC = AC = ACC = TC.{{sfnp|Clote|Kranakis|2002|p=12}}

We have <math>\mathsf{NC}^0 \subsetneq \mathsf{AC}^0 \subsetneq \mathsf{ACC}^{0}</math>. Specifically, PARITY is in <math>\mathsf{ACC}^0</math> but not in <math>\mathsf{AC}^0</math>.{{sfnp|Razborov|1987}} And since NC requires bounded fan-in, any function of type <math>\{0, 1\}^n \to \{0, 1\}</math> whose output depends on more than <math>O(1)</math> inputs is beyond <math>\mathsf{NC}^0</math>. In particular, the unbounded fan-in OR is beyond <math>\mathsf{NC}^0</math>.

In detail, define <math>f_n: \{0, 1\}^n \to \{0, 1\}</math> by <math>f_n(x_1, \dots, x_n) = \sum_i x_i \mod 2 </math>. Then it requires <math>\Omega(2^{\frac{n^{1 / d}}{16}})</math> gates to be computed by a <math>\mathsf{AC}^0 </math> circuit with depth <math>\leq d </math>.{{sfnp|Pitassi|2015}}

==Variations==

The power of the AC classes can be affected by adding additional gates.  If we add gates which calculate the [[modulo operation]] for some modulus ''m'', we have the classes [[ACC (complexity)|ACC<sup>i</sup>[m]]].{{sfnp|Clote|Kranakis|2002|p=12}}
